title: Oil Routes — supplemental strategic route overlays
geometry_policy: All geometry is schematic and follows named, source-supported corridor nodes. It is not live AIS, exact track alignment, pipeline alignment, or targeting-quality data.

routes.name: Red Sea / Suez energy shipping corridor
routes.note: Schematic Red Sea axis between Bab el-Mandeb and Suez. The corridor remains a major energy route, but 2026 traffic is affected by Houthi attacks, blockade threats and rerouting. This line does not represent a live vessel track.
sources: U.S. EIA — Red Sea attacks increase shipping times and freight rates
Reuters — Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb traffic update, Aug. 24, 2026

routes.name: Saudi East–West crude pipeline to Yanbu
routes.note: Schematic endpoint-to-endpoint representation of Saudi Arabia's existing East–West crude pipeline from the Abqaiq oil region to the Red Sea export system at Yanbu. It is not the surveyed pipeline alignment.
sources: Reuters — Saudi Arabia considers East–West pipeline expansion, July 7, 2026
U.S. EIA — World Oil Transit Chokepoints

routes.name: China–Iran rail corridor to Aprin
routes.note: Schematic rail corridor using source-supported nodes for the China–Kazakhstan–Turkmenistan–Iran route. The line shows strategic connectivity, not exact rail geometry or train position.
sources: Aprin Dry Port — Iran–China two-way freight train service launched
Aprin / IRNA — China–Iran–Europe rail corridor and Kazakhstan–Turkmenistan routing

routes.name: Russia–Iran eastern INSTC rail corridor to Aprin
routes.note: Schematic eastern INSTC route used by scheduled Russia–Iran freight via Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan and Incheh Borun. The line follows named corridor nodes and is not exact track geometry or a live train position.
sources: Aprin Dry Port — first scheduled freight train from Russia arrives at Aprin
N.Trans Lab — eastern branch of the International North–South Transport Corridor

coordinate_sources: Aprin Railway Station — Wikidata / RAI reference
